system_overview: This specification contains machine-checked formal proofs about the high-level specification of asynchronous termination detection. The proofs establish type correctness, safety (termination detection implies actual termination), stability (once terminated, the system stays terminated), and liveness (termination is eventually detected). The proofs are verified using the TLA+ Proof System (TLAPS).
actors_and_components: The system is the same ring of N nodes with pending messages as defined in the base AsyncTerminationDetection specification. This module focuses on proving properties rather than defining new behavior.
state_variables: All state variables are inherited from the base AsyncTerminationDetection specification: node activation status, pending message counts, and the termination detection flag.
initial_state: The initial state is inherited from the base specification.
actions: All actions are inherited from the base specification: terminate, send message, receive message, and detect termination.
safety_properties: Three properties are formally proved: (1) Type correctness: the type invariant is inductive. (2) Safety: the specification implies that whenever termination is detected, the system is actually terminated. (3) Stability/Quiescence: once the system terminates, it remains terminated permanently.
liveness_properties: Liveness is formally proved: if the system terminates, termination is eventually detected. The proof uses the enabledness condition of the detect termination action and the WF1 proof rule.
additional_assumptions: Requires TLAPS to be installed, specifically a build from a development branch with updated ENABLED/cdot support for the liveness proof. The standard TLAPS distribution will handle the safety proofs but will produce an error for the liveness proof. The proofs use multiple TLAPS backends including Zenon, Isabelle, and SMT solvers.
